stemMd:
A student has taken these notes:
- An old route map shows official roads.
- It omits informal paths.
- The map was commissioned to plan road maintenance.
- A historian warns that omission does not prove a path was unused.

The student wants to explain the historian's caution. Which choice is most effective?

options.label: A
options.textMd: A historian studied an old map.

options.label: B
options.textMd: Because the map served official road maintenance, omitted informal paths may fall outside its purpose rather than outside actual use.

options.label: C
options.textMd: The map proves that no informal paths existed.

explanationMd: The sentence connects document purpose to selective coverage. That connection explains why an absence on the map cannot automatically be interpreted as absence of use in the landscape.

distractorRationale.a: This gives no reason for the caution.
distractorRationale.d: This repeats a fact without explaining the inference limit.
